result.title: Which Parameters to Update? An Instance-Specific Adaptation Framework for Real-World Pansharpening
result.summary: Pansharpening aims to fuse a single observed image pair, comprising a low-resolution multispectral (LRMS) image and a panchromatic (PAN) image, to obtain a high-resolution multispectral (HRMS) image. Recently, deep learning-based methods have achieved significant performance due to their strong capability of extracting nonlinear features. However, distribution shifts between training data and test images can degrade the performance of pretrained pansharpening networks, limiting their generalization in real-world scenarios. In this work, we propose an instance-specific test-time adaptation framework that uses the observed PAN-LRMS pair to select and update only a subset of the pretrained network's parameters. Specifically, the framework uses cross-scoring to identify parameter groups whose updates improve reconstruction across image patches. It then updates the selected groups by minimizing a loss that combines a spectral consistency term with a newly designed spatial consistency term. Experiments show that the adapted networks perform better than their pretrained counterparts and outperform representative state-of-the-art pansharpening methods on GaoFen-2, QuickBird, and WorldView series datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 针对真实场景 pansharpening 中训练与测试分布偏移导致的性能退化，提出实例级测试时自适应框架：借助跨图像块的 cross-scoring 挑选预训练网络中值得更新的参数组，再用结合光谱一致性与新设计的空间一致性项的损失更新这些组。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按实例筛选参数子集、仅以一致性目标做测试时更新」的做法，可能为 LVR 中测试时状态/参数适配及「哪些更新真正贡献输出」的贡献分配提供可供核查的线索，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理或 latent 状态生成。
